<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="101.38px"/><col width="437.20px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="69.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BSY</span>: Busy</p><p class="TableIndent">This indicates that a flash memory operation is in progress. This is set on the beginning of a flash memory operation and reset when the operation finishes or when an error occurs.</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OPTVERR</span>: Option validity error </p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when the options read may not be the one configured by the user. If option haven’t been properly loaded, OPTVERR is set again after each system reset.</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by writing 1.</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 14</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RDERR</span>: PCROP read error </p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when an address to be read through the D-bus belongs to a read protected area of the flash (PCROP protection). An interrupt is generated if RDERRIE is set in FLASH_CR.</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by writing 1.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 13:10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="100.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 9</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FASTERR</span>: Fast programming error</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when a fast programming sequence (activated by FSTPG) is interrupted due to an error (alignment, size, write protection or data miss). The corresponding status bit (PGAERR, SIZERR, WRPERR or MISSERR) is set at the same time.</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by writing 1.</p></td></tr><tr height="100.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MISSERR</span>: Fast programming data miss error</p><p class="TableIndent">In Fast programming mode, 32 double words must be sent to flash successively, and the new data must be sent to the flash logic control before the current data is fully programmed. MISSERR is set by hardware when the new data is not present in time.</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by writing 1.</p></td></tr><tr height="116.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PGSERR</span>: Programming sequence error</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when a write access to the flash memory is performed by the code while PG or FSTPG have not been set previously. Set also by hardware when PROGERR, SIZERR, PGAERR, WRPERR, MISSERR or FASTERR is set due to a previous programming error.</p><p class="TableIndent">Set also when trying to perform bank erase when DBANK = 0.</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by writing 1.</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SIZERR</span>: Size error</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when the size of the access is a byte or half-word during a program or a fast program sequence. Only double word programming is allowed (consequently: word access).</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by writing 1.</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PGAERR</span>: Programming alignment error</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when the data to program cannot be contained in the same 64-bit flash memory row in case of standard programming, or if there is a change of page during fast programming.</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by writing 1.</p></td></tr><tr height="70.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">WRPERR</span>: Write protection error</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when an address to be erased/programmed belongs to a write-protected <span style="font-kerning:none;">part (by WRP, PCROP or RDP level 1) of the flash memory.</span></p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by writing 1.</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PROGERR</span>: Programming error</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when a double-word address to be programmed contains a value different from '0xFFFF FFFF FFFF FFFF' before programming, except if the data to write is '0x0000 0000 0000 0000'.</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by writing 1.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OPERR</span>: Operation error</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when a flash memory operation (program / erase) completes unsuccessfully.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set only if error interrupts are enabled (ERRIE = 1).</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by writing ‘1’.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">EOP</span>: End of operation</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when one or more flash memory operation (programming / erase) has been completed successfully. </p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set only if the end of operation interrupts are enabled (EOPIE = 1).</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by writing 1.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 3.7.6 Flash control register (FLASH\_CR)

Address offset: 0x14

Reset value: 0xC000 0000

Access: no wait state when no flash memory operation is on going, word, half-word and byte access

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="100.38px"/><col width="438.20px"/><tr height="84.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 31</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">LOCK</span><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">:</span> FLASH_CR lock</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set only. When set, the FLASH_CR register is locked. It is cleared by hardware after detecting the unlock sequence.<br/>In case of an unsuccessful unlock operation, this bit remains set until the next system reset.</p></td></tr><tr height="114.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 30</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OPTLOCK</span><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">:</span> Options lock</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set only. When set, all bits concerning user option in FLASH_CR register and so option page are locked. This bit is cleared by hardware after detecting the unlock sequence. The LOCK bit must be cleared before doing the unlock sequence for OPTLOCK bit.</p><p class="TableIndent">In case of an unsuccessful unlock operation, this bit remains set until the next reset.</p></td></tr><tr height="69.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 29</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SEC_PROT2</span>: Securable memory area protection bit for bank 2.</p><p class="TableBodyL">This bit is set to lock the access to the securable area in bank 2. It is set by software when exiting the securable area, and can only be written once. In case DBANK = 0, this bit is useless.</p></td></tr><tr height="66.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 28</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SEC_PROT1</span>: Securable memory area protection bit for bank 1. <br/>This bit is set to lock the access to the securable memory area for bank 1 (or when DBANK = 0). It is set by software when exiting the securable area, and can only be written once. </p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 27</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OBL_LAUNCH</span>: Force the option byte loading</p><p class="TableIndent">When set to 1, this bit forces the option byte reloading. This bit is cleared only when the option byte loading is complete. It cannot be written if OPTLOCK is set.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Option byte loading complete</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Option byte loading requested</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 26</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RDERRIE</span>: PCROP read error interrupt enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the interrupt generation when the RDERR bit in the FLASH_SR is set to 1.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: PCROP read error interrupt disabled<br/>1: PCROP read error interrupt enabled</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 25</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ERRIE</span>: error interrupt enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the interrupt generation when the OPERR bit in the FLASH_SR is set to 1.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: OPERR error interrupt disabled<br/>1: OPERR error interrupt enabled</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">EOPIE</span>: End of operation interrupt enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the interrupt generation when the EOP bit in the FLASH_SR is set to 1.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: EOP Interrupt disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: EOP Interrupt enabled</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 23:19</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 18</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FSTPG</span>: Fast programming</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Fast programming disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Fast programming enabled</p></td></tr><tr height="70.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OPTSTRT</span>: Options modification start</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit triggers an options operation when set.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set only by software, and is cleared when the BSY bit is cleared in FLASH_SR.</p></td></tr><tr height="100.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">START</span>: Start </p><p class="TableIndent">This bit triggers an erase operation when set. If MER1, MER2 and PER bits are reset and the STRT bit is set, an unpredictable behavior may occur without generating any error flag. This condition should be forbidden.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set only by software, and is cleared when the BSY bit is cleared in FLASH_SR.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MER2</span>: Bank 2 mass erase</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit triggers the bank 2 mass erase (all bank 2 user pages) when set.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 14:12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BKER</span>: Bank erase</p><p class="TableIndent">DBANK = 1</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Bank 1 is selected for page erase</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Bank 2 is selected for page erase</p><p class="TableIndent">DBANK = 0</p><p class="TableIndent">Reserved, must be at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="105.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 9:3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PNB[6:0]</span>: Page number selection</p><p class="TableBodyL">These bits select the page to erase:</p><p class="TableIndent">0000000:   page 0</p><p class="TableIndent">0000001:   page 1</p><p class="TableIndent">...</p><p class="TableIndent">1111111:   page 255</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MER1</span>: Bank 1 mass erase</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit triggers the bank 1 mass erase (all bank 1 user pages) when set.</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PER</span>: Page erase</p><p class="TableIndent">0: page erase disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: page erase enabled</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PG</span>: Programming</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Flash programming disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Flash programming enabled</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 3.7.7 Flash ECC register (FLASH\_ECCR)

Address offset: 0x18

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

Access: no wait state when no flash memory operation is on going, word, half-word and byte access

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="101.11px"/><col width="437.47px"/><tr height="178.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 31</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ECCD</span>: ECC detection</p><p class="TableIndent">DBANK = 1</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when two ECC errors have been detected (only if ECCC/ECCC2/ECCD/ ECCD2 are previously cleared). When this bit is set, a NMI is generated.</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by writing 1.</p><p class="TableIndent">DBANK = 0</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when two ECC errors have been detected on 64-bit LSB (bits 63:0) (only if ECCC/ECCC2/ECCD/ ECCD2 are previously cleared). When this bit is set, a NMI is generated.</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by writing 1.</p></td></tr><tr height="164.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 30</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ECCC</span>: ECC correction</p><p class="TableIndent">DBANK = 1</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when one ECC error has been detected and corrected (only if ECCC/ECCC2/ECCD/ECCD2 are previously cleared). An interrupt is generated if ECCCIE is set.</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by writing 1.</p><p class="TableIndent">DBANK = 0</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when one ECC error as been detected and corrected on 64-bit LSB (bits 63:0) (only if ECCC/ECCC2/ECCD/ ECCD2 are previously cleared).</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by writing 1.</p></td></tr><tr height="136.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 29</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ECCD2</span>: ECC2 detection</p><p class="TableIndent">DBANK = 0</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when two ECC errors have been detected on 64-bit MSB</p><p class="TableIndent">(bits127:64). This bit is set (only if ECCC/ECCC2/ECCD/ECCD2 are previously</p><p class="TableIndent">cleared). When this bit is set, a NMI is generated.</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by writing 1.</p><p class="TableIndent">DBANK = 1</p><p class="TableIndent">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="133.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 28</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ECCC2</span>: ECC correction</p><p class="TableIndent">DBANK = 0</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when one ECC error has been detected and corrected on 64-bit MSB (bits127:64). This bit is set (only if ECCC/ECCC2/ECCD/ECCD2 are previously cleared). An interrupt is generated if ECCCIE is set.</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by writing 1.</p><p class="TableIndent">DBANK = 1</p><p class="TableIndent">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 27:25</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="150.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ECCCIE</span>: ECC correction interrupt enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: ECCC interrupt disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: ECCC interrupt enabled.</p><p class="TableIndent">DBANK = 0</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the interrupt generation when the ECCC or ECCC2 bits in the FLASH_ECCR register are set.</p><p class="TableIndent">DBANK = 1</p><p class="TableBodyL">This bit enables the interrupt generation when the ECCC bit in the FLASH_ECCR register is set.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 23</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="54.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 22</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SYSF_ECC</span>: System flash ECC fail</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit indicates that the ECC error correction or double ECC error detection is located in the system flash.</p></td></tr><tr height="152.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 21</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BK_ECC</span>: ECC fail bank </p><p class="TableIndent">DBANK = 1</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit indicates which bank is concerned by the ECC error correction or by the </p><p class="TableIndent">double ECC error detection.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: bank 1</p><p class="TableIndent">1: bank 2</p><p class="TableIndent">DBANK = 0</p><p class="TableIndent">If SYSF_ECC is 1, it indicates which bank is concerned by the ECC error</p><p class="TableIndent">If SYSF_ECC is 0, reserved, must be kept cleared.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 20:19</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="117.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 18:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ADDR_ECC[18:0]</span>: ECC fail address</p><p class="TableIndent">DBANK = 0</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit indicates which address in the flash memory is concerned by the ECC error correction or by the double ECC error detection.</p><p class="TableIndent">DBANK = 1</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit indicates which address in the bank is concerned by the ECC error correction or by the double ECC error detection.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 3.7.8 Flash option register (FLASH\_OPTR)

Address offset: 0x20

Reset value: 0xFXXX XXXX. Register bits are loaded with values from flash memory at OBL.

Access: no wait state when no flash memory operation is on going, word, half-word and byte access

font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">:</span> BOR reset level</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits contain the VDD supply level threshold that activates/releases the reset. </p><p class="TableIndent">000: BOR level 0. Reset level threshold is around 1.7 V<br/>001: BOR level 1. Reset level threshold is around 2.0 V<br/>010: BOR level 2. Reset level threshold is around 2.2 V<br/>011: BOR level 3. Reset level threshold is around 2.5 V<br/>100: BOR level 4. Reset level threshold is around 2.8 V</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RDP</span><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">:</span> Read protection level</p><p class="TableIndent">0xAA: Level 0, read protection not active<br/>0xCC: Level 2, chip read protection active<br/>Others: Level 1, memories read protection active</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>Take care about PCROP_RDP configuration in Level 1. Refer to <a href="Embedded_flash_memory_%28FLASH%29_for_category_2_devices.htm#XREF_94262__Read_protection13" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Level 1: Read protection</a> for more details.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 3.7.9 Flash PCROP1 Start address register (FLASH\_PCROP1SR)

Address offset: 0x24

Reset value: 0xFFFF XXXX

Register bits are loaded with values from flash memory at OBL.

Access: no wait state when no flash memory operation is on going, word access.

### 3.7.10 Flash PCROP1 End address register (FLASH\_PCROP1ER)

Address offset: 0x28

Reset value: 0xX000 XXXX

Register bits are loaded with values from flash memory at OBL.

Access: no wait state when no flash memory operation is on going, word, half-word access. PCROP\_RDP bit can be accessed with byte access.

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="105.30px"/><col width="433.28px"/><tr height="116.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 31</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="Helv7" style="font-weight:Bold;font-size : 9.00pt;background-color:transparent;">PCROP_RDP</span><span style="font-weight:Bold;">:</span> PCROP area preserved when RDP level decreased</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set only. It is reset after a full mass erase due to a change of RDP from Level 1 to Level 0.</p><p class="TableIndent"><span class="Helv7" style="font-size : 9.00pt;background-color:transparent;">0: PCROP area is not erased when the RDP level is decreased from Level 1 to Level 0</span>. </p><p class="TableIndent">1: <span class="Helv7" style="font-size : 9.00pt;background-color:transparent;">PCROP area is erased when the RDP level is decreased from Level 1 to Level 0</span> (full mass erase).</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 30:15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 14:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="Helv7" style="font-weight:Bold;font-size : 9.00pt;background-color:transparent;">PCROP1_END</span><span style="font-weight:Bold;">[14:0]:</span> Bank 1 PCROP area end offset</p><p class="TableIndent">DBANK = 1</p><p class="TableIndent">PCROP1_END contains the last double-word of the bank 1 PCROP area. </p><p class="TableIndent">DBANK = 0</p><p class="TableIndent">PCROP1_END contains the last 2x double-word of the first PCROP area in all memory.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 3.7.11 Flash Bank 1 WRP area A address register (FLASH\_WRP1AR)

Address offset: 0x2C

Reset value: 0x00XX 00XX

Register bits are loaded with values from flash memory at OBL.

Access: no wait state when no flash memory operation is on going, word, half-word and byte access

### 3.7.12 Flash Bank 1 WRP area B address register (FLASH\_WRP1BR)

Address offset: 0x30

Reset value: 0x00XX 00XX

Register bits are loaded with values from flash memory at OBL.

Access: no wait state when no flash memory operation is on going, word, half-word and byte access

Address offset: 0x50

Reset value: 0x00XX 00XX

Access: no wait state when no flash memory operation is on going, word, half-word and byte access

### 3.7.17 Flash securable area bank1 register (FLASH\_SEC1R)

Address offset: 0x70

Reset value: 0xFFFX FFXX

Access: no wait state when no flash memory operation is on going, word, half-word and byte access

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="105.30px"/><col width="433.28px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="Helv7" style="font-weight:Bold;font-size : 9.00pt;background-color:transparent;">BOOT_LOCK</span><span style="font-weight:Bold;">: </span>used to force boot from user flash area.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Boot based on the pad/option bit configuration </p><p class="TableIndent">1: Boot forced from main flash memory </p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can be changed only in RDP level 0 or when doing a regression from RDP level 1 to level 0.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="100.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SEC_SIZE1[7:0]</span>: sets the number of pages used in the bank 1 securable memory area.</p><p class="TableIndent">Securable area starts at 0x0800 0000 and its size is SEC_SIZE1 * page size. This field can be changed in RDP level 0 only. </p><p class="TableIndent">Any attempt to modify inRDP level1 silently fails, and does not change register value.</p></td></tr></table></div>


<a id="XREF_93125__3_7_18_Flash_securable_area_bank2_register_(FLASH_SEC2R)13"></a>

### 3.7.18 Flash securable area bank2 register (FLASH\_SEC2R)

Address offset: 0x74

Reset value: 0xFFFF FFXX

Access: no wait state when no flash memory operation is on going, word, half-word and byte access.

Any attempt to modify in RDP level1 silently fails, and does change register value.</p></td></tr></table></div>
